note:
ALA-LC Tibetan Romanization Table, 2015 version (earlier versions: 2011, 1997), pp. 1-4; held source interscript-private-references/alalc/alalc-tibetan.pdf (the duplicate alalc-tibetan.pdf.pdf is byte-identical, same sha256). The table follows the Wylie transliteration system (Wylie 1959) with diacritics for non-Tibetan letters. Extraction: the PDF text layer is real Unicode text for the 30 consonant cells, the 9 non-Tibetan letter cells, the 4 sign cells (rjes su nga ro U+0F7E -> m-dot-below, sna ldan U+0F83 -> m+candrabindu, rnam bcad U+0F7F -> h-dot-below, paluta U+0F85 -> spacing grave), the notes, the numerals and the glosses; the 13 vowel-table cells, one cluster cell, and three note/example stack heads are PUA garbles. Every table row was cross-checked against rendered page images (300 dpi pages, 600 dpi cell crops).
Correction table (text layer -> print): the 13 vowel cells are PUA - U+F300 -> i-sign (U+0F72), U+F302 -> u (U+0F74), U+F303 -> e (U+0F7A), U+F304 -> o (U+0F7C), U+F5FA -> ii (U+0F73), U+F5FB -> uu (U+0F75), U+F5FC -> vocalic r (U+0F76), U+F5FD -> vocalic rr (U+0F77), U+F5FE -> vocalic l (U+0F78), U+F5FF -> vocalic ll (U+0F79; the only cell printed without a tsheg), U+F600 -> ai (U+0F7B), U+F602 -> au (U+0F7D), U+F5F9 -> a-chung (U+0F71) - each visually confirmed at 600 dpi in its carrier form plus tsheg; the t-sa cluster cell's letters are missing from the text layer (bare tsheg only; print = ta+sa stacked); the n-ya cluster cell is PUA U+F7AF (print = na+ya stacked); Note 7's example head (the sha-u-da-ddha stack) is PUA U+F755; Note 8's counter-cell (ga+subjoined ya) is PUA U+F360; the Punctuation 2 example's ba-ra-tsa stack is PUA U+F53F; the table cell for the a-chung letter prints a curly apostrophe (U+2019) where Note 3, the gloss and the map use the alif (U+02BC). Value codepoints verified identical print vs map for every romanization (r+ring-below, r+macron+ring, l+ring, l+ring+macron orders included).
Findings (map-vs-source; transcribed rows EXCLUDED from the generated tests, never forced green; record for the maps-fix pipeline):
1. STANDALONE ARTIFACTS (map-note-documented): the printed ཤ ས ཧ ཨ rows are sha sa ha a; the map encodes shaa saa haa aa (text-layer concatenation artifacts) - all four rows fail as printed.
2. ARTIFACT PROPAGATION (MAJOR, systematic consequence of 1): the combination grid's vowel rules for those 4 letters carry the artifact a - 9 vowel signs each, 36 rules: e.g. སོ -> sao (printed so), ཧེ -> hae (he), ཤོ -> shao (sho), ཨེ -> ae; the clean letters compose correctly (ཀེ -> ke, ཀཱ -> kā).
3. CLUSTER RULES UNREACHABLE (MAJOR): the three Note 8-9 disambiguation stacks གཡ ཏས ནཡ are present verbatim in the map (gʹya tʹsa nʹya, modified letter prime U+02B9) but never fire - the stage applies its parallel groups sequentially and the standalone-consonant group rewrites ga/ya/ta/sa/na first (runtime gaya tasaa naya); the map note's now-encoded claim does not hold at runtime. All three printed rows fail.
4. NON-TIBETAN STANDALONES (map-note-documented): ཥ ཛྷ ཌྷ (printed ṣa dzha ḍha) are not encoded as standalone base consonants (they exist only as subjoined grid members) and pass through - three rows fail.
5. NOTE 5: the reversed i ྀ (U+0F80) and reversed ii ཱྀ (U+0F81) have no rules; the print transcribes the reversed i the same as i.
6. NOTE 6: the reverse-d syllable-final scribal shorthand (ཌ for གས -> gs) is not encoded (contextual; no rule).
7. PUNCTUATION 2: the centered point (katakana middle dot U+30FB) indicating a space has no rule and leaks through.
8. PUNCTUATION 3: the angle brackets (guillemets) -> quotation marks rule has no map rules.
9. FINAL MARKS: the shad ། (and other sentence marks) have no rules and pass through unchanged; the print's example romanization omits them.
10. PUNCTUATION 2 EXAMPLE (འབའ・བསོད་བྷས་བརྩམས། -> ʼBaʼ Bsod-bhas brtsams): not reproducible - syllable-final འ is a bare alif (the map's standalone rule gives ʼa), syllable-initial capitalization and gloss hyphen division are caller-level, the implicit-a suppression in བསོད (bsod) is beyond the row rules, the ba-ra-tsa triple stack has no rule (the grid covers base+one subjoin; བ+ra -> bra fires, then the raw subjoined tsa passes through), and the U+30FB and shad leak.
11. NOTE 7 EXAMPLE (ཤུདྡྷོ྅ཧཾ -> shuddho`haṃ): composes as shau + ddhao + grave + haa + m-dot-below - the ཤ+u grid rule carries the artifact a, the ད+ddha grid rule keeps the final-member a and the following o-sign composes standalone (ddhao, printed ddho), and the ཧ artifact gives haa.
12. A-CHUNG ENCODING: the table cell prints a curly apostrophe (U+2019); Note 3, the gloss and the map use the alif (U+02BC) - map form kept, table/note inconsistency recorded.
13. MINOR: the map-only བྷ -> bha rule has no printed table row.
Inventory notes: the printed l-rubble-l-long cell (U+0F79) is the only vowel cell without a tsheg (transcription detail; the row passes); the ka cell is exactly hand test 1 and retained there; Note 1 (internal capitalization not followed) and Punctuation 1 (tsheg as hyphen/space; the map drops it - anomaly recorded in the map) are caller-level or already documented.
Bookkeeping: 73 printed rows transcribed; the rows array carries the 58 generated rows exactly; 12 rows are the findings above, excluded from generation; 2 passing rows dropped as exact duplicates of the tsa/nya consonant rows (the Note 9 letter-vs-stack demo cells; the stack sides of the demo are the t-sa / n-ya cluster rows themselves); 1 printed row (the ka cell) is the retained hand test 1. Regenerating via scripts/gen-row-tests.mjs from this artifact reproduces the embedded block byte-for-byte.
